# ARCore-Location

> Android library that places ARCore content at real-world coordinates (latitude, longitude, optional altitude). It uses ARCore's Geospatial API when the session has it enabled, and GPS plus compass otherwise. Java, minSdk 24, AndroidX, Java 17. Current version: 2.0.0.

Version 2.0 is a rewrite and most 1.x code no longer compiles. Common 1.x patterns to avoid: `new LocationMarker(longitude, latitude, node)`, `locationScene.processFrame(frame)`, `locationScene.mLocationMarkers.add(...)`, `new LocationScene(activity, arSceneView)`, `setRenderEvent`, `setBearingAdjustment`, `setAnchorRefreshInterval` and `ARLocationPermissionHelper`.

## Choosing a module

- `com.github.appoly.ARCore-Location:arcore-location:2.0.0` is the core. It works with any renderer and is the right choice for new apps.
- `com.github.appoly.ARCore-Location:arcore-location-sceneform:2.0.0` adds `LocationScene` and `LocationMarker` for Sceneform. Sceneform is archived and its native libraries are not 16 KB page aligned, so Google Play rejects apps targeting Android 15+ that include it. Use it only for apps that already use Sceneform.

Both come from JitPack: add `maven("https://jitpack.io")` to the repositories in `settings.gradle.kts`.

## Sceneform module

```java
LocationScene locationScene = new LocationScene(arSceneView);
getLifecycle().addObserver(locationScene); // starts, stops and cleans up; no per-frame call needed

LocationMarker marker = new LocationMarker(GeoCoordinate.of(51.50073, -0.12463), node) // latitude first
        .setHeight(1.5f) // metres above the camera, or above the coordinate's altitude when known
        .setOnRenderListener(m -> label.setText(Math.round(m.getDistanceMetres()) + " m"));
locationScene.addMarker(marker);
```

Options: `LocationScene.setMaxRenderDistanceMetres` (default 25, keep under 30), `setOverlapMode(OverlapMode.NONE | HIDE | STACK)`, `setMaxVisibleMarkers`; `LocationMarker.setOnlyRenderWhenWithinMetres`, `setScalingMode(ScalingMode.FIXED_SIZE_ON_SCREEN | NO_SCALING | GRADUAL_FIXED_SIZE | GRADUAL_TO_MAX_RENDER_DISTANCE)`.

## Core module with any renderer

```java
GeoTracker tracker = new GeoTracker(context);
getLifecycle().addObserver(tracker);

// Every frame, after session.update():
tracker.update(session, frame);
if (frame.getCamera().getTrackingState() == TrackingState.TRACKING && tracker.isReady()) {
    GeoPlacement p = tracker.place(target, frame.getCamera().getPose(), 25f, 0f);
    if (p != null) {
        // Create an anchor at (p.getWorldX(), p.getWorldY(), p.getWorldZ()).
        // Re-anchor only when this position moves more than about 0.3 m from the existing anchor.
    }
}
```

`tracker.getStatus()` is one of `STOPPED`, `WAITING_FOR_LOCATION`, `WAITING_FOR_HEADING`, `LOCATION_UNAVAILABLE`, `HEADING_UNAVAILABLE`, `LOCATION_STALE` or `TRACKING`. `tracker.getSource()` is `GEOSPATIAL` or `GPS_AND_COMPASS`.

## Permissions and Geospatial

Request `ArLocationPermissions.REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS` (camera, fine and coarse location) with an Activity Result launcher before starting AR. To use the Geospatial API, enable `Config.GeospatialMode.ENABLED` in the session config when `session.isGeospatialModeSupported(...)` is true, and set up an ARCore API key or keyless authorisation in Google Cloud. Without them the library falls back to GPS and compass automatically.

## Utilities

`GeoMath.distanceMetres(from, to)`, `GeoMath.bearingDegrees(from, to)` and `GeoMath.destination(start, bearingDegrees, metres)` take `GeoCoordinate`s.
